##### Extracurricular Reading

###### Instructions

1. Every day, translate elevated reading material from outside the LSAT, using the following sources:
	1. **[ScienceDaily.com](https://www.sciencedaily.com/)**
		1. Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by scientific language or fear science passages in RC
				2. Be sure to choose the articles that challenge you the most, not articles that look familiar or interesting
		2. **[Aeon.co](https://aeon.co/)**
		1. The most similar articles to LSAT RC on the internet
				2. Reading an Aeon.co article every day is a great habit if you have no specific topic-based weaknesses, but would like to make RC-style reading a habit.
		3. **[ALDaily.com](https://www.aldaily.com/)**
		1. Ideal daily reading for those who feel alienated by abstract language, art, humanities, and pretension.
				2. Be sure to choose the articles that look the most unfamiliar, not articles that speak to your pre-existing interests.
		4. **[NYT Guide to Essential Knowledge](https://www.amazon.com/York-Times-Guide-Essential-Knowledge-ebook/dp/B005EXS7E4/ref=tmm_kin_swatch_0)**
		1. The single best way to fix gaps in common knowledge
				2. Here is a list of sections in the Guide that are relevant to LSAT. If any of these topics would trouble you as an RC passage, read over that section of the guide.
				3. **LSAT Relevant Guide Sections**: Architecture, Zoology, Botany, History, Art, Photography, Literature, Music (the serious parts about jazz and blues, especially), Film, Dance, Drama, Climate & Weather and Glossary of Weather Words (In Geography), Government, Law, Philosophy, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Astronomy, Geology
		5. **[Crash Course](https://www.youtube.com/@crashcourse/playlists)**
		1. Not a written source, but Crash Course is too useful for solving common knowledge gaps to not include
				2. Watch Crash Course while you're in line, waiting for someone, on hold, brushing your teeth, etc. Any time you could be scrolling on your phone, watch Crash Course instead.
				3. **Top Five LSAT Relevant Crash Course Sections**: Intellectual Property (Ellen's favorite for LSAT students), Economics, US Government & Politics, Art History, and Philosophy

3

##### Vocab Training

##### Once A Week, Do This Instead

1

##### Translation Marathon

8 sections

≥ 1x per week

#### Ellen's Advice

##### Why Are We Doing This?

The Translation + CLIR Drills in this Routine are the foundation of your entire LSAT prep journey. This is the most important homework you will do during your LSAT prep training, even compared to PTs.

This Routine builds a foundation in LR Translation before we port your Translation skills over to RC in the next Routine.

##### How This Should Be Done

Your progression toward the Translation time and accuracy goals is primarily determined by two things: **volume** and **following the instructions.**

To maximize your progress in this Routine, do all your Translation + CLIR Drills consecutively; do not take breaks between Translation + CLIR Drills. Do not review your Translation + CLIR Drills in between sections. All review should be done in a separate sitting.

**Do at least 3 consecutive Translation + CLIR Drills per day, if possible.** Ideally, you would complete 6 Translation + CLIR drills consecutively per day. Doing 1 Translation + CLIR Drill per day will not improve your skills; it will keep your skills the same. You will only start improving on your second consecutive Translation + CLIR Drill; this is why it is so useful to do *at least* 3 consecutive Translation + CLIR Drills every day.

Add a Translation Marathon to your Daily Practice at least once per week. If you can manage to do Translation + CLIR Marathons more often, you will progress to the time goal faster.

Extracurricular Reading and Vocab should always be done at the end of your Routine to gradually expand your common sense in the subject areas where you're weakest. If you struggle with science passages, emphasize daily science engagement in the Extracurricular Reading. If you struggle with abstract language, emphasize daily humanities engagement in the Extracurricular Reading.

##### How to Move On

**Once you are halfway to your Translation + CLIR Drill time goal, move to the next Routine: Translation + Decaf.**

**The time goal for Translation + CLIR Drills is 20 minutes.** The accommodated time goals for Translation + CLIR Drills are 25 minutes for 53-minute accommodations and 30 minutes for 70-minute accommodations. Meeting this Translation + CLIR Drill time goal is only valid under two conditions: you have a CLIR for every stimulus and you have translated and quipped every stimulus in the section out loud. Ideally, you should hit -5 accuracy against the CLIR Answer Key consistently in order to beat the time goal, but this accuracy goal may be adjusted according to your score goals.

**Example of When to Move On**: You started at 52 minutes per out loud Translation + CLIR Drill section and you don't have accommodations, so your time goal is 20 minutes. The midpoint of 52 and 20 is 36, so you would move on when your time hits 36 minutes.

## How and Why to Do Decaf RC Translation

[Captured source](<../../raw/sources/old-obsidian-vault-2026-10-07/Clippings/loophole-online/training-camp/concept-review/How and Why to Do Decaf RC Translation • LO.md>) · SHA-256 `6abec7c63ea70c65cfdecbde9922d21b49a953a1ea9c78cfb7c92828b5dbcab7`

**Use boundary:** This is an attributed source explanation. Verify logical inferences independently and use current Joshua curriculum for student-facing delivery; source anecdotes and mechanism claims are not independently established.

##### Ellen's Notes

***Decaf RC Translation Drill***

**NOTE**: If you want to do your recaps out loud in the beginning to keep yourself honest about the quality and completeness of the recaps, that's totally fine. Transition to silent recaps when you feel like you're ready.

1. Read, translate, and quip paragraph 1. Do it just like LR.
	1. This means all the details are included just like they would be on LR.
		2. Quip after *every* Translation.
		3. This standard applies to every paragraph you ever translate on RC.
2. Look away from paragraph 1 and recap the **FULL TRANSLATION** of paragraph 1 silently.
	1. The recap is not a summary, gist, or main point.
		2. The recap should not omit names, dates, and lists.
		3. The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.
		4. It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.
		5. This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.
3. Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.
4. Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the **FULL TRANSLATION** of paragraph 2 silently.
5. Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.
6. Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.
7. Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the **FULL TRANSLATION** of paragraph 3 silently.
8. Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.
9. Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.

## How and Why to Use the Island

[Captured source](<../../raw/sources/old-obsidian-vault-2026-10-07/Clippings/loophole-online/training-camp/concept-review/How and Why to Use the Island • LO.md>) · SHA-256 `06ce12ef8cd1c1f9dfa8f013ffbcf96db30428d81114e9d6a53d8786bdbcee13`

**Use boundary:** This is an attributed source explanation. Verify logical inferences independently and use current Joshua curriculum for student-facing delivery; source anecdotes and mechanism claims are not independently established.

##### Ellen's Notes

***The Island***

**NOTE**: The Island is a spreadsheet you make yourself with one column called Island and another column called Canoed Away.

1. If a question is still mystifying after Camo, just add the citation of the question to the Island
	1. This means at least one of these three things is true:
		1. I don't understand why the right answer is right.
				2. I don't understand why the wrong answer is wrong.
				3. I have no idea how I could get this right in the future.
2. At the start of prep each day, spend 5 minutes on the Island retrying a question or two.
3. If the question clicks, move it to Canoed Away. Otherwise, keep it on the Island.

## Accuracy Failsafe

[Captured source](<../../raw/sources/old-obsidian-vault-2026-10-07/Clippings/loophole-online/workouts/Accuracy Failsafe • LO.md>) · SHA-256 `fbf73e13421835cd21de79ebff00e15b681a33d19b3b24639af6cfbaf29ef7be`

**Use boundary:** Immediate Camo after a five-minute break is an explicit exception to general delayed Camo. Related recovery drill names are pointers; full instructions were not captured.

#### Quick Facts

##### Will This Help Me?

This will help you if

You need a systematic way to improve your accuracy that will automatically assign you workouts to improve your habits when needed.

Skip for now if

You're nowhere near your accuracy goals.

challenge indexBuckle Up

levelIntermediate

minimum time90+ minutes

timing compatible with35m, 53m, 70m, Marathon, Stopwatch, Natural Pace

#### Instructions

**NOTE**: You can do an Accuracy Failsafe with any workout. Failsafes are time-training protocols that you can apply to any workout.

1. Set your accuracy goal as a target number of wrong answers per section.
	1. An accuracy goal could be -5, for example.
2. Complete an LR or RC section\* at your natural pace.
3. Take a five-minute break and Camo the section you just completed.
	1. If you have met your accuracy goal, proceed to a second section of the same type.
		1. This means if you just completed an RC section and hit your accuracy goal of -5, you would proceed to do another RC section with an accuracy goal of -5.
		2. If you have not met your accuracy goal on the first section, you have not beaten today's Failsafe.
		1. Do not decrease your target number of wrong answers tomorrow. Keep the same accuracy goal.
				2. Do not proceed to a second section of the same type today.
				3. Instead, Wrong Answer Journal and do one Recovery Workout (defined below) now.
4. If you have proceeded to a second section, take a five-minute break and Camo it.
5. If you have met your accuracy goal for the second time in a row, you have beaten today's Failsafe!
	1. Wrong Answer Journal both of today's sections.
		2. Decrease your target number of wrong answers tomorrow.
		1. This means that if you beat today's Failsafe of -5 accuracy, try for -4 accuracy on tomorrow's Failsafe.
6. If you do not meet the accuracy goal on the second section, you have not beaten today's Failsafe.
	1. Wrong Answer Journal both of today's sections.
		2. Do not decrease your target number of wrong answers tomorrow. Keep the same accuracy goal.
7. Return to Step 1 the following day.

Sections to use

New Sections Only

how to time

Count-Up Stopwatch

Countdown Timer

#### Ellen's Advice

##### If You Want to Win

- Failsafes are a great Workout for the student who loves data and structured goals.
- Don't be intimidated by all the steps you see in the Failsafe.
	- Once you get into it, the flow of the Workout is relatively intuitive.
		- Essentially, if you meet your goals twice in a row, you move your goal. If you don't meet your goals twice in a row, you don't move your goal.
- Which Recovery Workout should you choose?
	- It depends on where you tend to feel difficulty throughout the section.
		- If you notice you miss questions from not translating the answer choices, going toward an Answer Choice Primer or MemAC could be a great move.
		- If you notice that you are making strategic mistakes, making a Highlight Reel is a safe bet.
		- You can be the judge of which Recovery Workout is best for you, but the Recovery Workouts are designed to not allow you to simply repeat the exact same mistakes that you made in the first section of the FailSafe.
		- Even if you're tempted to go outside the list of Recovery Workout, don't do one that involves timed question answering.

## Camo Review

[Captured source](<../../raw/sources/old-obsidian-vault-2026-10-07/Clippings/loophole-online/workouts/Camo Review • LO.md>) · SHA-256 `fba42f6d9ca9d2fe7fce08c4be41ad96c7eb907f781eee2ad9622d7d6e612829`

**Use boundary:** Outcome labels are diagnostic clues. Never change an answer solely to game the mixture of misses/decoys. Platform UI claims are dated.

#### Quick Facts

##### Will This Help Me?

This will help you if

You are answering questions in any section and need to learn from your mistakes. (This is all of you 🕵🏻)

Skip for now if

You have not beaten the Translation + CLIR time and accuracy goals.

challenge indexPretty Chill

levelBeginner

minimum time15+ minutes

timing compatible withNot Timed

#### Instructions

1. When you finish an LR or RC section in LawHub, do not press Complete Section. Instead, write down your answers.
	1. Use Self-Paced Mode on all LR and RC sections. Never use Exam Mode.
2. At least 24 hours later, enter your answers into Camo Review.
	1. **Do not check your answers against the answer key before entering your answers into Camo Review.**
3. Camo Review will give you a list of questions to return to.
	1. This list includes all of your wrong answers and an unknown number of decoy correct answers.
4. Reattempt all of the questions in your Camo Review from scratch. Attempt to do a better job on the question now than you did the first time.
	1. Doing a better job means you should retranslate, requip, and re-CLIR the stimulus on LR or retranslate and requip the passage on RC. Retranslate every part of the question, consider every answer choice, and try to correct your process mistakes before choosing a new answer.
5. Enter all your new answers into Camo Review.
6. Camo Review will identify all your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, Self-Doubt, and Self-Confidence answers.
7. Your Misreads, Conceptual Gaps, and Self-Doubt answers have been automatically added to your Wrong Answer Journal. Go to your Wrong Answer Journal now to immediately begin the Wrong Answer Journal process.

video walkthrough

[How to Camo](https://new.theloophole.com/training-camp/browse/stage/accuracy/video/how-to-camo)

Sections to use

Previously Seen Sections Only

how to time

Untimed

#### Ellen's Advice

##### If You Want to Win

- Never Camo before doing your sections for the day. Always Camo as the last LSAT thing you do for the day.
	- If you Camo immediately before completing another section, you will be overly reactive to the result.
		- If the previous day's section went well, this can make you lazy.
		- If it went poorly, this can make you discouraged.
		- It's not worth taking the risk of either of these reactions affecting your performance on the next section.
- The only point of Camo Review is to get a -0.
	- Do not phone in the Camo Review or rechoose the answer you originally chose out of loyalty because you aren't sure it's wrong.
		- If you got more than two questions back in the Camo Review, some of the questions are definitely wrong, so you must change at least some of them.
- Do not Camo a section immediately after completing it, unless you are directed explicitly to do so as part of another Workout or Routine.
	- If you Camo a section immediately after completing it, the Camo score will be worse and you will lose a valuable opportunity to improve.

		3. The recap should not be a shopping list of information. It should be a story in your own words.
		4. It is encouraged to mix up the order of the sentences and ideas.
		5. This standard applies to every paragraph (or collection of paragraphs) you ever recap on RC.
3. Read, translate, and quip paragraph 2. Do it just like LR.
4. Look away from paragraph 2 and recap the **FULL TRANSLATION** of paragraph 2 silently.
5. Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 back to back silently.
6. Read, translate, and quip paragraph 3. Do it just like LR.
7. Look away from paragraph 3 and recap the **FULL TRANSLATION** of paragraph 3 silently.
8. Without looking back, recap the Translations of paragraphs 1 + 2 + 3 back to back silently.
9. Repeat this pattern for all remaining paragraphs.
10. Complete this same process on all remaining passages in the section.

per passage time goal to move on

12 min (outloud recaps), 8 min (silent recaps)

#### Ellen's Advice

##### If You Want to Win

- If you have a 70-minute time accommodation, you can use Decaf RC Translation on test day. You do not have to master Cappuccino RC Translation and Caffeinated RC Translation for use on test day, if Decaf RC Translation offers superior Translation retention.

Sections to use

how to time

Count-Up Stopwatch

#### Ellen's Advice

##### If You Want to Win

- **It is very important that you do not take breaks between sections or check your sections in the middle of the Marathon.**
	- Marathons only work because your brain doesn’t get the chance to re-adapt to non-LSAT thinking.
		- Taking breaks guarantees that the Marathon will not work.
		- Do not check your phone.
				- Do not have conversations.
				- Do not take a lunch break.
		- Put snacks and drinks on the desk to eat while you Marathon, if needed.
		- The only breaks allowed during Translation Marathons are medically required or biologically required breaks.
		- Running to the bathroom is allowed between sections.
				- Accommodated breaks for medically required tasks (like insulin injections, etc) are obviously allowed.
- Open all the sections you plan to complete in separate tabs before starting the Translation Marathon.
- Keep track of the order of the sections in your Translation Marathon, so you can analyze the results.
- If you feel yourself getting worse as the Translation Marathon progresses, you are likely becoming fatigued.
	- This is not cause for alarm. Fatigue is part of the process; it indicates that you need to build stamina.
- At the end of the Translation Marathon, take a break and then check all the sections against the CLIR Answer Key in a big batch.

##### Timing Tips

- Set a section timer for 400 minutes in LawHub's Self-Paced Mode. **Do not use Exam Mode.**
- Time each Translation + CLIR Drill with an external stopwatch. Record the time each drill takes in your tracker.

#### Ellen's Advice

##### If You Want to Win

- Don't simply memorize the correct diagrams. Diagram each statement fresh every time.
- Change the letters in the statements.
- You're working too hard to lose points on your real LSAT because you didn't really get Unless.

##### Timing Tips

- It shouldn't take you more than five seconds to diagram an individual Unless statement once you really understand how Unless works.
- The entire Routine shouldn't take you more than 15 seconds total once you're trained
	- I just diagrammed three Unless statements in 9 seconds to prove it can be done.
- If the Unless Practice Routine takes you much longer than 15 seconds, it just shows how much you need to do it
- Once you hit the point where you can diagram three Unless statements in 15 seconds, you can lower your Unless Practice Routine frequency to once per week.

<a id="wrong-answer-journal"></a>

## Wrong Answer Journal

[Captured source](<../../raw/sources/old-obsidian-vault-2026-10-07/Clippings/loophole-online/workouts/Wrong Answer Journal • LO.md>) · SHA-256 `30513ab4adc6a393a6a5cfa24f759d1189f5ce173e590e5749966bd611e6afba`

**Use boundary:** This is an attributed source explanation. Verify logical inferences independently and use current Joshua curriculum for student-facing delivery; source anecdotes and mechanism claims are not independently established.

#### Quick Facts

##### Will This Help Me?

This will help you if

You need to improve your accuracy and stop making the same mistakes over and over again.

Skip for now if

Wrong Answer Journals are harmless.

challenge indexPretty Chill

levelBeginner

minimum time15+ minutes

timing compatible withNot Timed

#### Instructions

1. After you've Camoed your LR or RC section, begin the Wrong Answer Journaling process.
2. For each wrong answer, fill in the date you did the section, the question number that was wrong, and the answer you chose.
	1. This information will already be filled in for you if you Camo using Loophole Online.
3. Fill in your Reason Missed column
	1. In this column, write down **what you did wrong that caused you to miss this question**.
		1. Ask yourself, "Why did I think that this wrong answer was right? Why did I think that this right answer was wrong?" Focus on changing the actions that enabled these mistaken judgments.
		2. The first word of every entry in this column should be "I."
		1. Example: "I misidentified the question stem."
				2. This will force you to reflect on **what you did** that caused you to choose the wrong answer and overlook the right answer.
4. Fill in your Solution column
	1. In this column, write down **what you will do differently to ensure you don't make this same mistake again**.
		1. Ask yourself, "What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the wrong answer is wrong? What could I have done that would have made me realize in the moment that the right answer is right?"
		2. The first words of every entry in this column should be "I will..."
		1. Example: "I will do Question Stem Training to improve my ability to correctly identify question types."
		3. Frame your Solution Column as a direct response to the Reason Missed column.

Click [here](https://new.theloophole.com/review-and-camo/wrong-answer-journal) to go to your Wrong Answer Journal

Sections to use

how to time

Untimed

#### Ellen's Advice

##### If You Want to Win

- Keep your Wrong Answer Journal entries short and sweet. One to two sentences is enough for each column.
- **Do not waste time in your Wrong Answer Journal writing down detailed explanations of why the answer you chose was wrong, and why the right answer is right in the exact context of the question.**
	- If you're writing anything that cannot be ported directly to subsequent sections, you are wasting your Wrong Answer Journal time.
- The Wrong Answer Journal gives you a chance to identify the exact **actions you took** that made you make the wrong decision. It then gives you the opportunity to decide which actions you will take in the future that will enable you to make correct decisions. This is the essence of improvement on the LSAT.
	- I want you to know why an answer is right and another is wrong, but I don't want you to stop there. I want you to start there.
		- After you know why the correct answer is correct and why the wrong answer is wrong, look more deeply at your actions and mindset in relation to the question.
		- What did you do that caused this result? And what will you do to ensure a different result next time?
- Do not rely on cheap explanations in your Reason Missed column like "silly mistake," "misread," or "rushing."
	- Dive into why you made this silly mistake, why you misread, and why you were rushing.
		- This is how you can identify the problematic actions that lead to problematic judgments and change them for the better.
